newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco industry settles Mississippi lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco industry settles Mississippi lawsuit.

text.p: Mississippi Attorney General Mike Moore and the tobacco industry settled the state's lawsuit seeking to recover money spent on treating smoking-related illness, a spokesman for Moore said on Thursday.
Details of the settlement were not disclosed but the spokesman, Trey Bobinger, said the pact was consistent with the broader accord reached between cigarette makers and the states last month.

Bobinger, an aide to Moore, said the attorney general would hold a news conference in Jackson, Miss., on Thursday afternoon to announce the deal. Moore's office said on Wednesday that the attorney general had given the industry until Thursday to agree to a settlement or go to trial.

Mississippi's suit, which was scheduled to go to trial next Wednesday in Pascagoula, would have been the first of the state cases to be tried. Officials in 40 states have sued the industry to recoup the state costs of treating smoking-related illnesses.

Although the states and the industry reached a landmark $368.5 billion settlement last month that included some health care concessions from cigarette makers, the accord has been criticised as too lenient by some members of Congress.
The settlement must be approved by Congress, and with its fate uncertain, the states must settle their Medicaid lawsuits individually or go to trial.
Bobinger said that if the broader pact does not survive, "this (settlement) protects our position, it protects the people of Mississippi."
Bobinger added that Moore believed the national settlement would pass Congress in a form similar to that agreed on in June by the attorneys general and the industry.
Most tobacco stocks rallied on the news of the Mississippi settlement.
